name: jira.js
description: Modern Jira REST API client for JavaScript & TypeScript — Jira Cloud API v2/v3, Agile & Service Desk. Type-safe, tree-shakable, works in Node.js and browsers (ESM/CJS).

paragraphs: JavaScript / TypeScript library for Node.js and browsers to interact with Atlassian Jira APIs
Jira.js is a TypeScript client for the Atlassian Jira REST APIs — Jira Cloud and self-hosted Jira Data Center — for Node.js and browsers. It covers eleven surfaces, in eight groups:
features: Jira Cloud platform API - issues, projects, fields, workflows
Jira Agile API - sprints, boards, backlog
Jira Service Management API - requests, queues, organizations
Assets API - the configuration management database, on Cloud and Data Center alike
Teams API - teams, their members and external links, at organization level

whatItDoes.text: JavaScript / TypeScript library for Node.js and browsers to interact with Atlassian Jira APIs

requirements.text: Provide refresh credentials and the client refreshes the access token before expiry (and on 401), collapses concurrent refreshes into one call, persists the rotated refresh token via onTokenRefresh, and routes requests through the API gateway ( — so no host is needed. clientSecret and refresh are server-side only.

A: Yes, since 6.3, on both deployments. createAssetsClient covers the Assets Cloud REST API — it takes a workspaceId and its own configuration, because Assets answers on api.atlassian.com rather than on your site. createAssetsServerClient covers the self-hosted one and takes the same client as every other Data Center surface.
